question: For a drug to permeate through the cornea, you must:

options.opc: Join the lysozyme that is present in the tear fluid.
options.opd: Present a certain lipophilicity and a minimum degree of water solubility.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Drug" -> "certain lipophilicity" -> "permeate lipid layers of cornea" -> "minimum degree of water solubility" -> "pass through aqueous layers" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Drug" -> "weak acid character" -> "partially ionized at physiological pH" -> "balance between lipophilicity and hydrophilicity" -> "enhanced corneal permeability" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Drug" -> "very high polarity" -> "limited lipid solubility" -> "reduced corneal permeability" -> 40%
CHAIN: "Drug" -> "totally ionized" -> "high water solubility" -> "poor lipid solubility" -> "reduced corneal permeability" -> 30%
CHAIN: "Drug" -> "join lysozyme in tear fluid" -> "possible interaction with tear proteins" -> "unclear effect on corneal permeability" -> 50%
analysis: For a drug to effectively permeate through the cornea, it needs to have a balance between lipophilicity and hydrophilicity. The corneal epithelium is lipophilic, while the stroma is more hydrophilic. Therefore, a drug must have certain lipophilicity to pass through the epithelium and a minimum degree of water solubility to traverse the stroma. This balance allows the drug to effectively penetrate the corneal layers.
